## 🌍 World politics & geopolitics

- <a id="st-9fa21cc3d182" class="st-a"></a>**France's economy shrank by 0.1% in the third quarter, after zero growth in the second, according to the first estimate published by the statistics institute INSEE on Friday 30 October.** Economists had expected slight growth. Household spending rose by 0.4% and public spending by 0.3%. Investment fell for a second quarter, by 0.6%, and exports dropped 1.7%, so trade took 0.6 points off growth. INSEE's provisional estimate puts October inflation at 3.4% year on year, up from 3.1% in September, with energy prices rising for the fourth month in a row. Economy minister Roland Lescure told Franceinfo that "the French economy is at a standstill" and said that without the budget savings in the 2027 budget "we will hit the wall", according to Le Monde. Le Monde also notes that those cuts could weaken household purchasing power further. A small downward revision of the second quarter, due at the end of November, would put France into technical recession, defined as two quarters of contraction in a row. [INSEE, 30 Oct 2026](https://www.insee.fr/fr/statistiques/9111036) [new source] `[official PR]` · [INSEE inflation flash, 30 Oct 2026](https://www.insee.fr/fr/statistiques/9107965) [new source] · [Le Monde, 30 Oct 2026](https://www.lemonde.fr/economie/article/2026/10/30/recul-surprise-du-pib-au-troisieme-trimestre-l-economie-francaise-flirte-avec-la-recession_6802918_3234.html)
  Why it matters: France is one of Switzerland's main trading partners. Shrinking output combined with rising inflation in the eurozone's second-largest economy narrows the room for both the government's budget plans and the ECB.
